title: Natural comparison of etale object cohomology with cohomology on open subschemes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $q\in\mathbb N$. Let $P$ be the actual degree-$q$ object-cohomology presheaf of $F$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], whose values are Ext from the sheafified free abelian representables and whose maps are induced by representable morphisms. For every open $U\subseteq X$ with inclusion $j_U$ [def-weil-open-immersion], there exist isomorphisms $e_U:P(U)\simeq H^q(U_{et},j_U^{-1}F)$, simultaneously natural for all inclusions $i:V\hookrightarrow U$: $e_V\circ P(i)=H^q(c_{i,j_U}^{-1})\circ i^*\circ e_U$, with the pullback and composition comparison of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. No point of X, colimit diagram, or local-scheme continuity is asserted.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution of the abelian etale sheaf F. Ext from the sheafified free abelian representable at U is cohomology of this resolution evaluated at U, by the free-sheaf and Yoneda adjunctions and Ext via an injective resolution. Restriction to U preserves injectives because it has exact extension by zero as left adjoint. The inverse-image/localization comparison therefore identifies this section complex with the restricted injective resolution on U. Taking cohomology gives the displayed isomorphism e_U. This construction is independent of the chosen injective resolution by the comparison theorem for Ext.

For V contained in U, the unit identity for open restriction identifies the pullback of a section with its restriction. Apply it with g equal to the inclusion of U into X and W equal to V. The fibre product V times_X U is V; the identity unit cancels with its identity comparison. Thus the two successive restriction isomorphisms, followed by the inverse-image composition comparison, equal the direct restriction isomorphism for V. Apply this identity degreewise to the injective resolution and take cohomology. It gives precisely the naturality equation for e.

theorem etaleOpenObjectCohomology_natural
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (q : ℕ)
    (P : X.Etaleᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hP : P = (Functor.flip ((uliftYoneda.{u + 1} ⋙
      (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj AddCommGrpCat.free ⋙
      presheafToSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).op ⋙
        Abelian.extFunctor q)).obj F)
 :
    ∃ e : ∀ U : X.Opens, P.obj
        (op (Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι)) ≅
        AddCommGrpCat.of (Sheaf.H ((Etale.upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj F) q),
      (∀ (U V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ U),
        P.map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (P := @Etale) (Q := ⊤) (X := X)
              (A := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι) (X.homOfLE h)
              (X.homOfLE_ι h) trivial).op ≫
            (e V).hom =
          (e U).hom ≫ AddCommGrpCat.ofHom
            (Etale.cohomologyMap (X.homOfLE h)
              ((Etale.upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj F) q) ≫
            AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (Sheaf.H.map
              ((Etale.upperStarComp AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (X.homOfLE h) U.ι V.ι
                (X.homOfLE_ι h).symm).inv.app F) q))
